rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px re-inspected: severe oni elder faces viewer with two open hands withdrawing, robe hangs freely from deeply sagging/splintering Eryoju branch without human pulling; judgement weight clear. One head/two eyes/two arms, opaque robe, no horns or anatomy invented. Empty robe and stressed branch dominate with elder, river secondary; uncanny judicial act reads at 200px. No torture/victims/text/aura. Seven Sangar checks pass; ordinary-laundry first attempt archived.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face, hands and branch crops. One head, two eyes, two open five-fingered hands, a coarse opaque robe, a splintered bending branch with an empty pale robe hanging from it, moonlit river: the anatomy count and modesty are fine. But Keneo is documented as an underworld ONI (keneo-c01) and an 'oni-formed old man' (c08), and here he is an entirely ordinary bearded old man in a rough robe. His expression reads as startled or pleading, not as a fierce underworld judge. At 200px the image reads as 'old man gesturing at a sheet on a tree', which is the 'ordinary man' rejection of Uji Sangar #7. The weight-of-sin effect (c05/c08) is only partly legible: the branch is thick and splintered at the top, but its sag does not clearly read as being pulled down by the robe.

correction_notes: Redraw Keneo with the documented oni form (keneo-c01/c08), not an ordinary old man. A fierce oni elder face (glaring eyes, bared teeth, coarse dark-red or weathered oni skin, wild hair) is supported by 'oni-formed old man'. If small oni horns are used, record them in artistic_choices as the interpretation of c08. Make his expression severe and judging, not startled. Show the robe taken from a dead soul (c03) hanging from a thin branch of the great Eryoju tree that bends visibly and strongly under the robe's weight alone, as the measure of sin (c05/c08), by the Sanzu River (c01). Keep a fully opaque robe, no torture or victims, and no text or aura.
